environment.sandbox: private dir under /tmp, deleted after run

checks.title: 100-destination fixture: immediate filtering; scrolling; latency recorded

assertions.desc: selection followed 30 Down presses through the scrolled list
harness precondition: filter counts 100 -> 19 -> 1 -> 0 are strictly decreasing (no stale reads)

open_contract_questions: Q1 meta for a signal-killed child: contract gives exit_code int|null and signal int|null; harness gates only on signal==9 and launched==true and records exit_code (non-gating).
Q2 argv bytes that are not valid UTF-8: contract says byte-for-byte for text with spaces/quotes/non-ASCII; harness records non-UTF-8 argv preservation as non-gating.

Q3 SIGINT sent to the whole foreground process group reaches the child directly and via forwarding; the contract does not define the acceptable delivery count; harness gates only on the child's exit status and records the count.
Q4 SIGTERM during the TUI: contract names no exit code; harness gates on prompt exit and terminal restoration only.
Q5 Agent connection closed by the peer before any reply byte (EOF with zero bytes): UNAVAILABLE vs PROTOCOL_ERROR is undefined, so it is not tested.
Q6 ANSI escapes inside agent comments: contract bans ANSI escapes in JSON strings but does not say whether agent-provided comments are sanitised; not tested (a raw ESC is not sent by the fake agent).
Q7 Behaviour of profile show without --json is undefined; not tested.
not_covered: native Windows (named pipe, CommandLineToArgvW, console Ctrl-C)

limitations: Windows is NOT covered: named-pipe agent path, CommandLineToArgvW quoting, console Ctrl-C and ConPTY behaviour need a native Windows run (blocked_on: native Windows host).
WSL is NOT covered (blocked_on: Windows host with WSL).
Harness is POSIX-only and ran on one OS/arch (see environment); other Unix variants (Linux pty/AF_UNIX semantics) are untested here.

TUI is judged through a pty plus the pyte VT emulator, which answers DA and cursor-position queries but not OSC colour/XTVERSION/kitty-keyboard queries (a framework that waits for those answers will show a slower first frame); real terminal emulators may differ. stdout and the TUI frames share the tty, so stdout-vs-stderr separation of TUI output cannot be proven; SELECTED is verified as the text after the alternate screen is left.
Restoration after a panic/uncaught exception cannot be induced black-box and is NOT tested; only select, quit, Ctrl-C (also in filter mode) and SIGTERM paths are.

'No network' and 'no shell invocation' (contract section 1) cannot be proven black-box; only observable effects are tested (no shell metacharacter expansion, sentinel files, no fake-agent contact, no stray files).
Allocation behaviour ('never allocate from an untrusted length first') is inferred from fast, correct failure on 0x7fffffff / nkeys 100000 frames, not measured.
Timing thresholds (500 ms SIGINT, 100 ms resize, 2 s malformed-agent failure) are wall-clock on a possibly loaded machine; resize uses best-of-3.
Invalid UTF-8 handling is tested with a single 0xFF byte (one U+FFFD); runs of invalid bytes are deliberately not tested because the contract does not define replacement-character counting.
The disposable keys are generated per run, private halves deleted immediately; fingerprints are cross-checked against /usr/bin/ssh-keygen -lf.
